blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
When goods cross a border, they often meet taxes. These taxes have names like duties, tariffs, or customs taxes. The importing country decides how much to charge. It is usually a percentage of the declared value of the goods.

The rate depends on two things: what the goods are and where they come from. Some countries have free trade agreements. These agreements lower or remove the taxes for certain goods. Other countries use tariffs to protect their local industries from foreign competition.

For a business that imports or exports, these taxes are part of the real cost of every shipment. You must understand them before the goods arrive, not after the container is at the port. This is the first rule of international trade.

items.q: Who decides how much tax to charge on the goods?
options: The company that makes the goods
items.why: "The importing country decides how much to charge."

items.q: The tax rate depends on…
options: the weight of the container only
what the goods are and where they come from
items.why: "The rate depends on… what the goods are and where they come from."

items.q: What do free trade agreements do?
options: They lower or remove taxes for certain goods
items.why: "These agreements lower or remove the taxes for certain goods."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with this idea:
options: It is fine to check the tax after the container is at the port.
The rate can change from country to country.
Taxes are part of the real cost of a shipment.
You should learn the tax before the goods arrive.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz para entender o imposto ANTES da chegada — checar só depois é o erro que ele critica.

items.q: Why do some countries use tariffs? This suggests that…
options: they do not like international trade at all
they want to help foreign companies grow
they want to protect their own local businesses
they want to remove all taxes
items.why: Inferência: "tariffs to protect their local industries from foreign competition" — a tarifa defende a empresa de dentro do país.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver ajudando um novo exportador. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi, thanks for sending me the numbers. Let's look at your shipment to Brazil together.

Your price is good, but we have to add one more thing: the import duty. In Brazil, the customer pays this tax when the goods arrive. It is a percentage of the declared value. So if your value on paper is low, the duty is low. If it is high, the duty is high.

Here is the important part. Many new exporters forget this tax. They send a great price, and then the customer sees the final cost with the duty, and they say no. That is a bad surprise. You must tell the customer the full landed cost from the start.

Let me show you. The product, the shipping, and the duty — you add them all together. That is the real cost. This is not the cheapest number, but it is the honest number. And an honest number keeps the customer happy for the next order too.

So before you send your next quote, always check the duty first. Do not wait for the container to reach the port.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What extra cost does Oliver want to add to the price?
items.why: "we have to add one more thing: the import duty."

items.q: In Brazil, who pays the import duty when the goods arrive?
items.why: "the customer pays this tax when the goods arrive."

items.q: Why does Oliver say the low price can be a "bad surprise"?
options: Because the price is wrong on paper
Because the customer sees the higher final cost and says no
Because the exporter loses the container
items.why: Inferência: se a tarifa não aparece no começo, o cliente descobre o custo total depois e recusa.

items.q: What does Oliver mean by the "honest number"?
options: The price only the exporter can see
The full cost with product, shipping and duty together
items.why: Inferência: ele soma produto, frete e imposto — o custo real, não o mais barato.

items.q: What is Oliver's main advice to the exporter?
options: Check the duty before sending the next quote
Lower the declared value to pay less
Never talk about taxes with the customer
Wait for the container to reach the port
items.why: "before you send your next quote, always check the duty first."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The customer paid a duty on the goods." A duty is…
items.why: Duty = imposto de importação.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The government put a high ___ on foreign steel to protect local factories."
items.why: Tariff = tarifa, o imposto usado para proteger a indústria local.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Our company buys coffee from Colombia. We ___ it every month."
items.why: To import = importar: trazer os produtos de outro país.

items.q: "The declared value was 10,000 dollars." The declared value is…
options: the price written on paper for the goods
items.why: Declared value = valor declarado dos produtos, usado para calcular o imposto.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The ___ left the port yesterday and will arrive next week."
items.why: Shipment = remessa: os produtos enviados juntos.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns no comércio internacional. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager must sign off on the new shipment." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We will roll out the product in three countries this year." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = lançar, colocar em uso.

items.q: "The customer pushed back on the high price." This means the customer…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar.

items.q: "Please fill out the customs form before the goods leave." To fill out means to…
items.why: Fill out = preencher (um formulário).

items.q: "The tax added a lot to the price, so the deal fell through." To fall through means to…
items.why: Fall through = fracassar, não se concretizar.
